messages:
maria: Heads up — EU ingest is ~20m behind for 03/20 01:00-02:00 UTC. Small window but affects agg-hours. Need an operator-safe runbook to recompute just the affected shards without stomping quotas.
aj: on it. do we know which tenant shards? small size sounds like targeted recompute ok.
sam: shard ids: eu-1a eu-1b. Estimated 3M events total. risk: double-count if prefix cache not invalidated.
paul: +1 to targeted. We should NOT use the high-priority bypass token unless SRE okays it. Prefer canary -> estimate -> scale.
maria: agreed. SRE wants a short script that does: estimate cost -> dry-run -> run with quota-aware routing. Also needs to mark job for dashboard visibility.
aj: rough operator script (internal runbook snippet):
```
# estimate
curl -sS -X POST https://internal-console/api/recompute/estimate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPERATOR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"shards":["eu-1a","eu-1b"],"start":"2026-03-20T01:00:00Z","end":"2026-03-20T02:00:00Z"}'

# dry-run
curl -sS -X POST https://internal-console/api/recompute/dry_run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPERATOR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"shards":["eu-1a"],"force":false}'

# kick off (quota-aware)
curl -sS -X POST https://internal-console/api/recompute/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPERATOR_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"shards":["eu-1a","eu-1b"],"priority":"canary","max_parallel":2}'
```
sam: couple notes: (1) add `invalidate_prefix_cache=true` for tenant-level aggregates so we don't double-count; (2) route through the reserved pool in eu-region, not default shared pool, to keep latency predictable.
paul: console UX ask: show estimate token cost inline when operator hovers over `Run` and show which routing pool will be used. Makes approval faster.
aj: re: invalidate prefix cache — ops only. We need to ensure recompute job marks which prefixes it touched so the cache invalidation job can be idempotent.
maria: SRE approval pending. tagging SRE: @sre-team — can we get exception to use reserved eu pool for this one-hour backfill? We'll follow canary then ramp.
ops-bot: job estimate request received: est_id=est-20260320-01, queued for 1m.
paul: also add a safety: if the estimate > 5k token-units, auto-abort and require manual sign-off.
aj: good guardrail. I'll add `--max-estimate=5000` to the operator script.
sam: minor internal API debate: should the dry_run endpoint be separate, or a `?dry_run=true` flag on run? Separate endpoints make auditing easier.
maria: auditability matters. separate endpoints + persisted estimate record is better.
ops-bot: dry-run completed: dryrun_id=dr-20260320-01, simulated 0 writes, will impact 0 cache keys (per simulation).
aj: starting canary run on eu-1a now with max_parallel=1. posting job id.
ops-bot: job queued: job_id=rb-8621 (shard=eu-1a, priority=canary)
sam: watching logs. if we see prefix-cache hits after writes, abort and run invalidate job manually.
paul: once canary good, ramp to eu-1b with max_parallel=2. also update console dashboard with a temporary tile: "recompute: 03/20 01:00-02:00 (eu)" so product and cs can see.
maria: thanks. can someone file a small UX ticket to surface estimate tokens on the recompute modal? idempotency and cache flags should be visible.
aj: filing UX ticket now (UX-1187). I'll push script to runbook and link to ticket.
ops-bot: job succeeded: rb-8621 completed in 42s, 0 write collisions, aggregated delta within expected variance.
maria: moving to run eu-1b. will follow the script and keep SRE in loop. :thumbsup:
sam: nice. afterwards let's capture the prompt sets that triggered regressions so Optimize can flag future regressions.
paul: and we should add a console guard that prevents `priority=bypass` unless a specific SRE override code is provided.
maria: agreed. closing the loop once eu-1b done. thanks all. :heart:
